newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia oil export seen flat to up 10 pct - executive.
newsitem.headline: Russia oil export seen flat to up 10 pct - executive.

text.p: Russian crude oil exports outside the Commonwealth of Independent States in 1997 will be at least flat on 1996's two million barrels per day (bpd), and may rise to 2.2 million bpd, a Russian oil executive said on Wednesday.

Mikhail Gaikazov, executive adviser to oil trading company Nafta-Moskva, also said during a break at an energy conference that Russian oil output this year could slip about one percent on 1996's 6.03 million bpd.

"The only factors affecting exports will be pipeline capacity constraints and the weather," he said, referring to storms which often shut the Black Sea export outlet of Novorossiisk. "We'll export as much as the infrastructure can handle."
Oil production would stop slipping altogether year-on-year in 1998, he said. Russian oil output showed double digit declines in the first years of this decade but began levelling off last year.

Gaikazov said Russian non-CIS oil exports last year were worth around $13.6 billion. Exports to the CIS, which were around 446,000 bpd and accounted for about 20 percent of total oil exports, brought in 30 percent less revenue per barrel than did non-CIS deliveries.
